tasks.task: Mobilise site and establish site setup
tasks.scope: Establish site office, welfare facilities, toolbox talk location. Brief all personnel on occupied residential protocol, Kiora Lane and courtyard access restrictions, and Leo and Associates hold-point approvals process.
hazards: Failure to communicate occupied residential protocol — occupant or worker injury from unauthorised access or disturbance
Inadequate toolbox talk briefing — workers unaware of site-specific hazards, access restrictions, or hold-point process
Site office or welfare facility location creates trip or access hazard in occupied building
tasks.dominant_hazard: Failure to communicate occupied residential protocol — occupant or worker injury from unauthorised access or disturbance
controls: Brief all workers and occupants on occupied residential protocol before any site activity starts.
Display site access map at site office showing Kiora Lane and courtyard restricted zones and worker entry points.
Conduct toolbox talk covering occupied building rules, hold-point approval process, and Leo and Associates contact details.
Locate site office and welfare facilities outside occupied residential areas or obtain written occupant consent before use.
Confirm all workers hold current White Card (CPCCWHS1001) and have read the site-specific induction pack.
Establish a hold-point register at site office to log all Leo and Associates approvals required for elevated work.
Brief all workers on noise and dust management restrictions applicable to occupied building hours.
Post site rules and emergency contact details at site office, welfare area, and main entry point.
Notify building occupants / body corporate / strata manager of work schedule, access restrictions, and expected noise/dust at least 48 hours before work starts
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start any elevated work until: Leo and Associates has signed the hold-point register and confirmed scaffold erection and working-at-heights permits are in place.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow workers or plant into occupied areas until: site office has briefed all personnel on occupant access restrictions and obtained signed acknowledgement.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start work until: written notification delivered to all affected occupants and body corporate/strata manager
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any worker enters Kiora Lane or courtyard without written Leo and Associates approval or site office authorisation.
🛑 STOP WORK if: toolbox talk or occupied residential protocol briefing has not been delivered to new workers before they enter site.
🛑 STOP WORK if: site office or welfare facilities are located in occupied residential areas without documented occupant written consent.
admin: Obtain and file occupant consent letter before locating site facilities in or near occupied building.
Prepare site induction pack specific to occupied residential protocol and Leo and Associates hold-point process.
Create and maintain hold-point register at site office — record date, approval, approver name, and permit reference.
Establish daily toolbox talk schedule and confirm attendance of all site personnel.
Provide Leo and Associates contact details (name, phone, email) to all workers at induction.
Record White Card and current competency evidence for all workers in site records before commencement.
Residents responsible for clearing personal items, furniture, potted plants, and non-common fixtures from balcony and work areas before each phase — area left/excluded if not cleared
Temporary access to neighbouring properties required — confirm access arrangements before commencing
Vegetation trimmed away from surfaces designated for painting or remedial works prior to commencement — area excluded if vegetation impedes access
On-site parking or provision of parking permits required for duration of works
Final inspection and agreed scope of works to be confirmed before commencement
ppe: Hard hat — all site personnel on entry.
High-visibility vest — all site personnel in occupied building or courtyard areas.

monitoring.critical_control: Exclusion zone barriers complete, signage visible, access controlled
monitoring.frequency: before each shift start
monitoring.evidence: Barriers intact, signage legible, no unauthorised entry
monitoring.what_to_look_for: Barriers intact, signage legible, no unauthorised entry

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues

tasks.task: Erect scaffold over Kiora Lane and courtyard
tasks.scope: Install fully braced scaffold to balconies via Kiora Lane and courtyard access. Scaffold inspection and certification before any work commences. All working heights over 4m.
hazards: Fall from height — worker falls during erection, particularly over Kiora Lane with live pedestrian or vehicle access below
Scaffold collapse or structural failure — incomplete bracing, defective components, or overload during erection
Scaffold strikes vehicle or pedestrian on Kiora Lane — inadequate traffic control or clearance
Worker struck by scaffold component — dropped item during erection or component failure
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — worker falls during erection, particularly over Kiora Lane with live pedestrian or vehicle access below
controls: Verify licenced scaffolder has completed load calculations and design drawings before erection starts.
Barricade Kiora Lane footpath and vehicle access with traffic control signs and barriers until scaffold fully braced and certified.
Install working platform edge protection (guardrail, toe board, mid-rail) as each level rises — do not allow workers to stand on incomplete platforms.
Secure all scaffold components with retaining pins or clips — check each connection before and after loading.
Tag completed scaffold with handover certificate only after independent check confirms all bracing, ties, and footings are secure.
Conduct daily visual check of scaffold before work starts — stop work if any component is loose, cracked, bent, or missing.
Isolate scaffold from Kiora Lane traffic with vehicle-rated barriers and maintain 2m clearance minimum to prevent strikes.
Brief all workers on erection sequence, load limits, and emergency procedures before work starts — confirm understanding verbally.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start erection until: licenced scaffolder has approved site setup, footings, and access path in writing
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow any worker onto completed scaffold until: independent checker has inspected and signed handover certificate confirming all safety requirements met
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any scaffold component is loose, cracked, bent, corroded, or missing — do not remove or adjust until licenced scaffolder re-inspects
🛑 STOP WORK if: traffic barrier is moved, damaged, or removed from Kiora Lane — do not resume until barrier is restored and pedestrian/vehicle exclusion confirmed
🛑 STOP WORK if: workers are observed standing on incomplete platforms without full edge protection in place
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain signed scaffold erection permit from licenced scaffolder before any component is positioned on site.
Obtain handover certificate from independent checker before any worker accesses the scaffold — retain on site for duration of use.
Obtain working at heights permit signed by supervisor before elevated work commences.
Obtain noise management plan from site manager — confirm occupancy notification completed for residents in courtyard.
Record daily scaffold condition check in site log — note any repairs, adjustments, or component replacements.
tell Kiora Lane occupants and business operators of scaffold erection dates, traffic controls, and duration.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Wear Class D hard hat — mandatory always on scaffold.
Wear high-visibility clothing — orange or yellow vest or jacket visible from all angles.
Wear steel-capped boots with good grip and ankle support.
Wear fall harness (tested within 12 months) when working at leading edges before guardrails are installed — secure lanyard to independent anchor point.

monitoring.critical_control: Check that all pins are installed, guardrails are secure, and no platforms are incomplete before worker access.
monitoring.frequency: Before erection starts, after each work shift, before handover, and daily during use
monitoring.evidence: Signed erection permit, handover certificate, daily condition check log, photo record of bracing and edge protection installation

responsibility.SUP: Verify scaffold or EWP certification, supervise erection, sign off load checks
responsibility.WKR: Follow erection plan, wear harness at height, report defects

tasks.task: Remove existing membrane, screed and tile bed
tasks.scope: Strip existing waterproofing membrane, screed and tile bed from balcony slabs. Contains silica dust generation. Contain and remove all demolition waste. No disturbance of occupied spaces below.
hazards: Inhalation of silica dust — dry cutting or sweeping of screed and tile bed without adequate dust control
Struck by falling debris — tile fragments, screed or membrane pieces fall onto Kiora Lane or courtyard below
tasks.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of silica dust — dry cutting or sweeping of screed and tile bed without adequate dust control
controls: Wet all surfaces with low-pressure water spray before cutting or breaking screed and tile bed.
Use dust extraction vacuum (HEPA-filtered) connected to angle grinder or breaker during active cutting.
Sweep only damp surfaces — do not dry sweep screed or tile dust.
Direct all waste into sealed skip or labelled containers — do not drop loose debris over edge.
Check scaffold tag and handover certificate before starting work — do not proceed if missing or expired.
Barricade balcony edge and any gaps in temporary barriers with 1.2 m high solid fencing.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start cutting or breaking until: temporary polythene containment is installed and sealed, HEPA vacuum is tested and operational, and water supply is confirmed connected and working.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: water supply fails or HEPA vacuum loses suction — do not continue dry work.
🛑 STOP WORK if: polythene containment tears or gap appears — stop cutting immediately and repair or re-seal.
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker notices dust cloud visible beyond temporary barrier — investigate and reposition vacuum or increase water suppression.
admin: Obtain and display scaffold erection permit (licenced scaffolder signature) before any worker access.
Obtain working at heights permit (supervisor signature) for each shift working at height.
Verify all workers hold current White Card (CPCCWHS1001) — check induction card on-site before task briefing.
Verify scaffolder holds current licence class for this scaffold type and height — sight certificate before erection.
Verify workers have completed SDS training for waterproofing membrane product — record attendance on site.
Record names and induction times on site register — maintain until project completion.
Arrange noise monitoring if work affects occupied units — provide findings to site supervisor daily.
tell building occupants 48 hours before work starts — include dust and noise impact notice.
ppe: Respiratory protective equipment (RPE) — Type P2 or P3 particulate respirator fitted and tested to wearer each shift.
Hearing protection — earplugs or muffs (level determined by noise assessment).

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: before each use and continuous during work
monitoring.evidence: Visual confirmation of water mist on surface, audible vacuum operation, no visible dust cloud, scaffold tag present and dated, handover certificate visible on-site, polythene barrier intact.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove existing membrane, screed and
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove existing membrane, screed and per SWMS

tasks.scope: check slab for cracks, spalling and structural defects. Repair cracks by grind-and-fill or injection. Hold point: Leo and Associates to check and approve substrate condition before membrane application commences.
hazards: Fall from height — worker on balcony during inspection, grinding or injection work without adequate edge protection
Struck by grinding wheel or tool — angle grinder failure, binding or kickback during crack grinding
Inhalation of concrete dust — dry grinding without water suppression or dust extraction
Injection injection pressure hazard — chemical injection under pressure strikes worker or pressurised line ruptures
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — worker on balcony during inspection, grinding or injection work without adequate edge protection
controls: Verify Leo and Associates structural inspection and written approval of substrate condition before any repair work starts.
Install compliant edge protection or guardrail at balcony perimeter — minimum 1.1 m high, tested and tagged before worker access.
Use wet grinding with integral water suppression on all concrete crack grinding — no dry grinding permitted.
Connect dust extraction to angle grinder — maintain continuous airflow during grinding operations.
Secure angle grinder with certified anti-rotation device — check wheel binding risk before each use.
Review chemical injection SDS and confirm ventilation adequate for application location — stop if airflow insufficient.
Brief all workers on balcony fall hazard, edge location, and injection pressure hazard before task start.
Assign spotter to monitor worker position near edge during grinding and injection work.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start grinding or injection until: scaffolding handover certificate provided and edge protection verified by site supervisor.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply membrane until: Leo and Associates substrate inspection report signed and all repairs documented.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: worker positioned within 1 m of unprotected balcony edge without harness tensioned.
🛑 STOP WORK if: angle grinder shows wheel binding, vibration, or eccentric rotation during operation.
🛑 STOP WORK if: water suppression system fails during grinding or dust extraction airflow ceases.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain and file scaffold erection permit signed by licensed scaffolder before scaffold assembly.
Obtain scaffold handover certificate from licensed scaffolder — file before any worker access.
Obtain working at heights permit for this task — sign before inspection, grinding or injection commences.
Obtain noise management plan if grinding duration exceeds 2 hours or affects occupants.
Verify workers hold current White Card (CPCCWHS1001) and Working at Heights competency (RIIOHS204E or equivalent).
Verify site supervisor holds scaffolding licence class appropriate to scaffold height and type.
Record substrate inspection results, repair method, and Leo and Associates approval in project file.
Brief occupants of noise and dust during grinding — confirm access restrictions posted at balcony entry.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
ppe: Class D harness with shock absorber
Respiratory protection (P2 or P3 mask) for grinding dust — upgrade to powered respirator if continuous grinding >4 hours
Hearing protection (earplugs or muffs) if grinding noise exceeds 85 dB(A)

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.frequency: continuous during all elevated work on balcony
monitoring.evidence: Site log or supervisor sign-off documenting harness check and tether attachment per shift.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Investigate and repair slab substrate
responsibility.WKR: Perform Investigate and repair slab substrate per SWMS

tasks.scope: Apply new waterproofing membrane system to repaired slab as per engineer specification. Cure and test per specification before screed application.
hazards: Fall from height — worker on balcony during membrane application, particularly at edges
Slipping or loss of balance — wet or primed slab surface becomes slippery; membrane application solvent or primer reduces slip resistance
Inhalation of membrane or primer fumes — inadequate ventilation or respiratory protection during application of solvent-based or volatile system
Chemical skin or eye contact — membrane or primer splashes during application or cleaning
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — worker on balcony during membrane application, particularly at edges
controls: Obtain and review SDS for membrane and primer before work starts; brief all workers on hazards, application method, and ventilation requirements.
Establish continuous mechanical ventilation across the slab during application and for 2 hours after; open all available windows and doors to occupied spaces below.
Apply membrane only in calm conditions — stop application if wind exceeds 15 km/h or if spray drift reaches occupied areas below.
Wear respiratory protection (P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) with organic vapour cartridge) during primer and membrane application; replace cartridges per SDS or if odour detected.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves and eye protection; change gloves immediately if contact occurs.
Damp-wipe or cover wet membrane surfaces with non-slip matting to prevent slipping during cure; restrict worker movement to matting pathways only.
Install edge protection (aluminium angle or temporary mesh barrier) at all balcony edges and openings before membrane work starts; confirm no gaps or overlaps.
Rig full-body harness to certified anchor point before working within 2 m of any edge; do not remove harness until work in that zone is complete.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply screed until: Leo and Associates (engineer) has inspected and signed off membrane cure, bond strength, and test results per specification.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any worker shows signs of chemical exposure (nausea, dizziness, headache, eye irritation) — evacuate and seek medical advice immediately.
🛑 STOP WORK if: wind speed exceeds 15 km/h or spray reaches occupied areas; resume only when conditions improve.
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold tag is missing, expired, or handover certificate cannot be produced.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Brief workers on occupied building protocols; no application during peak hours 7–9 am, 5–6 pm.
Confirm EPA licence and waste disposal contractor details before delivery.
Record membrane lot number, application date, primer type, and cure completion in site diary.
Provide SDS and method statement to occupants 48 hours before work; post warning signs.
Arrange independent moisture and bond testing per engineer specification before hold point sign-off.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
ppe: P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) with organic vapour cartridge (type per SDS)
Full-body harness (certified, inspected, appropriate anchorage point)

monitoring.critical_control: SDS on site, PPE matched to chemical, ventilation confirmed
monitoring.frequency: start of each application shift and before each balcony zone entry
monitoring.evidence: Harness rigged to anchor point, cartridge installed, worker demonstrating fit and comfort of respirator

responsibility.SUP: Supervise membrane application, verify controls in place, sign off hold points and engineer inspection
responsibility.WKR: Apply membrane per SWMS, use PPE, report chemical exposure or hazards, comply with all controls

tasks.scope: Barricade balconies and affected slab areas. Install signage and restrict occupant access. Establish safe pedestrian routes around scaffold footprint in courtyard and Kiora Lane access.
hazards: Fall from height — occupant or worker passes under or around incomplete barricade on balcony or slab edge
Pedestrian struck by debris from work area — inadequate barricade or signage allows foot traffic in fall zone
Trip hazard from barricade materials or inadequate ground-level signage in courtyard or Kiora Lane
Occupant access to work area — barricade failure or unlocked access allows entry to hazardous zone
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — occupant or worker passes under or around incomplete barricade on balcony or slab edge
controls: Barricade all balcony edges and slab perimeters with rigid barriers minimum 1.1 m high before any worker enters the work zone.
Install prohibition signs (No Entry — Hazardous Work Zone) at minimum 2 m intervals and at all pedestrian approach points on balconies and slab edges.
Establish continuous pedestrian routes around scaffold footprint in courtyard and Kiora Lane access — mark with high-visibility tape and directional signage.
Lock all access points to barricaded balconies and slab areas — designate one supervised entry point with sign-in log for authorised workers only.
Check barricade integrity and signage visibility daily before work starts — fix or replace any damaged, loose, or obscured barriers immediately.
Brief all occupants on prohibited zones and safe pedestrian routes — post notices in common areas and provide written notice to each affected residence.
Remove trip hazards from ground-level barricade materials — position barriers tight to edges and secure loose fittings or feet.
Conduct daily site walk with supervisor to confirm barricades remain intact, signage remains visible, and occupant access is restricted.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow any worker or occupant access to barricaded zones until: barricade integrity check is signed off by site supervisor and all signage is installed and visible.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any barricade is broken, collapsed, or partially removed and occupants or workers have access to the fall zone.
🛑 STOP WORK if: any access point to a barricaded balcony or slab edge is unlocked or unattended.
🛑 STOP WORK if: signage is missing, obscured, or unreadable at any pedestrian approach point.
admin: Obtain Scaffold Erection Permit signed by licenced scaffolder before barricade installation.
Obtain Handover Certificate from scaffolder before any worker uses completed barricade.
Obtain Working at Heights Permit before work at height commences.
Complete occupant notification letter — distribute to all affected residences before barricade installation.
Record daily barricade inspection checks in site logbook — supervisor signature required.
Record occupant complaints or access breaches and remedial action in incident log.
ppe: High-visibility vest (Day-glo orange or yellow) when installing barricades at height.

monitoring.critical_control: Check barricade integrity and signage visibility are complete before worker entry each shift.
monitoring.frequency: Daily before work start and after any maintenance or occupant activity
monitoring.evidence: Daily checklist signed in site logbook — note barricade condition, signage status, access point locks, and trip hazards clear.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Isolate and barricade work areas
responsibility.WKR: Perform Isolate and barricade work areas per SWMS

tasks.task: Make good and reinstate occupied spaces
tasks.scope: Remove protective coverings. Clean and reinstate common areas, access routes and courtyard. Remove temporary signage. Confirm occupant access fully restored and space safe for reoccupancy.
hazards: Occupant or worker struck by falling protective covering — inadequate removal or coverage collapse
Trip hazard from protective coverings, debris or temporary materials during reinstatement
Inadequate cleaning — dust, chemical residue or debris left on access routes or common areas hazards to occupants
tasks.dominant_hazard: Occupant or worker struck by falling protective covering — inadequate removal or coverage collapse
controls: Remove protective coverings in sections — support each section before removing adjacent section to prevent collapse.
Lower each section of covering to ground using controlled descent — never drop or allow free fall.
Check coverings for tears, damage or contamination before removal — stop work if structural failure or hazmat suspected.
Sweep and vacuum all dust and debris from access routes and common areas before occupant return.
Wipe down hard surfaces in access routes with damp cloth to remove residual dust and chemical residue.
Remove all temporary signage, barricades and delineation markers from reinstated areas.
Brief occupants on any residual site activity or access restrictions before full handover.
Conduct final walk-through with site supervisor and occupant representative — confirm all hazards cleared and space safe for reoccupancy.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow occupant re-entry until: Site supervisor and occupant representative complete final walk-through and confirm all protective coverings removed, debris cleared, and hazards eliminated.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: protective covering shows signs of structural failure, tears, or collapse during removal.
🛑 STOP WORK if: chemical residue, visible contamination, or hazmat suspected on surfaces or coverings.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupants present in work area during removal of protective coverings or debris clearance.
admin: Obtain EPA licence confirmation before work starts — job involves removal of protective membranes in occupied building.
Confirm noise management plan in place and occupants notified of removal schedule.
Record final walk-through inspection and occupant sign-off on site diary.
Provide occupants with contact number for post-handover defect reporting.
ppe: Dust mask P2 — during sweeping and cleaning of residual dust

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.frequency: before each rectification session
monitoring.evidence: Signed defect list, photographic record, specification document on site
monitoring.what_to_look_for: Signed defect list, photographic record, specification document on site

responsibility.SUP: Verify fall protection, check module weights, sign off hold points
responsibility.WKR: Wear fall harness, check lanyard attachment, report equipment damage

tasks.scope: Apply screed to fall and finish. Retile balcony surfaces. Reinstate balustrades and edge trims to specification. Conduct final defect inspection before handover.
hazards: Fall from height — worker on balcony during screed placement, tiling or balustrade reinstallation, especially before balustrade completion
Struck by screed pump or tile saw — equipment malfunction, runaway hose or blade failure
Manual handling injury — lifting screed bags, tiles, balustrade panels or edge trims
Trip hazard from scaffold, wet screed, dropped tiles or temporary materials on balcony
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — worker on balcony during screed placement, tiling or balustrade reinstallation, especially before balustrade completion
controls: Verify scaffold handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder before any worker accesses balcony.
Confirm working at heights permit signed and current before starting screed, tiling or balustrade work.
Install perimeter edge protection (guardrail or certified fall arrest system) on all open edges before screed application.
Barricade wet screed and fresh tile surfaces with temporary fencing — keep exclusion zone 1m from wet edge.
Position screed pump on stable, level ground with pressure hose secured and checked for damage before each use.
Brief workers on wet slip hazard and trip risks from scaffold, hoses, dropped tiles and temporary materials at shift start.
Wear harness and lanyard attached to certified anchorage point when working within 2m of unprotected edge or incomplete balustrade.
Lift screed bags and tile boxes with mechanical aid where available — maximum 20kg manual load per worker.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply screed until: perimeter edge protection installed and inspected by supervisor.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not reinstate balustrade until: all screed and tile work complete and surfaces cured or set to specification.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: harness or lanyard detaches or damage visible during work at height.
🛑 STOP WORK if: screed pump hose ruptures, leaks pressurised product, or shows signs of failure.
🛑 STOP WORK if: balcony surface is saturated or slip risk is present and cannot be isolated.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain copy of scaffold erection permit and handover certificate — file on site before work starts.
Verify working at heights competency and white card current for all workers — names and expiry dates recorded.
Review SDS for screed membrane product — brief workers on handling, ventilation and skin contact controls.
Establish exclusion zone signage around wet screed and tiling work — inform building occupants of temporary access restrictions.
Conduct final defect inspection with supervisor — record on checklist: edge protection integrity, balustrade alignment, tile adhesion, trim finish, surface curing time.
ppe: Safety harness and certified lanyard (when working within 2m of unprotected edge)
Respirator or dust mask (P2 minimum when cutting dry tile or screed)

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: before each shift start and before each elevated task on balcony
monitoring.evidence: Scaffold tag visible, handover certificate on file, harness inspection log with date and worker initials

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Install screed, tiles and balustrades
responsibility.WKR: Perform Install screed, tiles and balustrades per SWMS

tasks.scope: Dismantle and remove all scaffold from Kiora Lane and courtyard. Certification on removal. Leave site clear of all temporary structures.
hazards: Fall from height — worker falls during scaffold dismantling, particularly over Kiora Lane or courtyard
Scaffold collapse during dismantling — incomplete or incorrect removal sequence causes remaining structure instability
Struck by falling scaffold component — dropped tube, clamp, board or brace during removal
Pedestrian or vehicle struck on Kiora Lane — scaffold component falls or collapses onto traffic below
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — worker falls during scaffold dismantling, particularly over Kiora Lane or courtyard
controls: Obtain signed scaffold dismantling plan from licensed scaffolder before any removal starts.
Brief all workers on dismantling sequence and designated drop zones before work commences each day.
Barricade Kiora Lane below scaffold to exclude pedestrian and vehicle traffic during removal.
Remove scaffold components in reverse erection sequence — top to bottom, working from one end.
Secure each removed component immediately to prevent rolling or shifting on platform.
Tag removed scaffold as 'unsafe for reuse' if bent, cracked or deformed.
Lower all components to ground using rope and pulley — do not drop or throw.
Verify all fixings and connections are released before moving or removing any component.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start dismantling until: licensed scaffolder has reviewed site conditions and signed dismantling plan
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove final components until: licensed scaffolder has inspected remaining structure for stability and signed removal certificate
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any component falls or is dropped onto Kiora Lane or occupied areas below
🛑 STOP WORK if: remaining scaffold shows visible movement, sag, twist or cracking during removal
🛑 STOP WORK if: barricade or exclusion zone is breached by pedestrian or vehicle traffic
admin: Obtain and verify signed scaffold dismantling plan from licensed scaffolder before work start.
Verify all workers hold current White Card and Scaffolding Licence appropriate to scaffold class and height.
Verify all workers hold current Working at Heights competency (RIIOHS204E or equivalent).
Brief site occupants on dismantling schedule, noise, and exclusion zones 24 hours before work.
Record daily dismantling progress, any structural concerns, and licensed scaffolder inspections in site diary.
Obtain and file final removal certificate from licensed scaffolder confirming all scaffold removed and site clear.
ppe: Wear full-body harness with inertia reel lanyard secured to fixed anchor point — test anchor before use.
Wear steel-capped boots with ankle support.

monitoring.critical_control: Licensed scaffolder verifies dismantling sequence and remaining structure stability daily.
monitoring.frequency: Before each day's removal work and before final sign-off
monitoring.evidence: Signed dismantling plan, daily inspection notes, final removal certificate filed

responsibility.SUP: Verify scaffold or EWP certification, supervise erection, sign off load checks
responsibility.WKR: Follow erection plan, wear harness at height, report defects

tasks.scope: Remove site office, welfare facilities and all plant. Dispose of waste. Final site inspection and sign-off. Restore Kiora Lane and courtyard to pre-works condition.
hazards: Manual handling injury — removing site office, welfare facility components, plant or waste materials
Vehicle struck or struck by vehicle — plant movement in confined Kiora Lane or courtyard during removal
Trip hazard from temporary structures, plant or waste during demobilisation
tasks.dominant_hazard: Manual handling injury — removing site office, welfare facility components, plant or waste materials
controls: Plan removal sequence with Site Supervisor before starting — identify heavy items, access routes, and staging areas in Kiora Lane and courtyard
Barricade Kiora Lane and courtyard to exclude vehicles and occupants during plant movement and waste removal
Brief all workers on manual handling before removing site office or welfare components — use team lift for items over 20 kg
Use mechanical handling (forklift, telehandler or crane) for items over 50 kg — do not hand-carry large panels, furniture or equipment
Load waste into skip bin or licensed waste truck — confirm waste type matches EPA disposal requirements before removal from site
Clear temporary structures, cables, hoses and debris from all walking areas before final inspection — remove trip hazards
Conduct final walkover of Kiora Lane and courtyard with Site Supervisor and building occupant representative — photograph pre-works condition baseline for comparison
Restore Kiora Lane and courtyard surfaces to pre-works condition — repair damage, remove temporary markings, clean dust and debris
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove site office or welfare facility until: Site Supervisor confirms all hazardous materials (asbestos, lead, chemicals) have been identified and removed by licensed contractor if applicable

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not sign off final inspection until: building occupant representative and Site Supervisor confirm Kiora Lane and courtyard match pre-works condition, and all plant, waste and temporary structures are removed
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: vehicle or plant movement in Kiora Lane or courtyard strikes occupant, causes near-miss, or barricade is breached
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker attempts to hand-carry item weighing over 20 kg or drops load during manual handling in occupied building area
🛑 STOP WORK if: waste removal includes unlicensed or unidentified hazardous material without EPA compliance documentation
admin: Obtain EPA waste disposal licence or confirm licensed waste contractor before removing waste from site
Record final site inspection photographs and sign-off sheet — Site Supervisor and building occupant representative signatures required
Verify all plant, temporary structures and waste removed from Kiora Lane and courtyard before site vacation
Confirm all utilities (power, water, temporary services) isolated and disabled — record on site handover form

monitoring.critical_control: Exclusion zone barriers complete, signage visible, access controlled
monitoring.frequency: before each shift start
monitoring.evidence: Barriers intact, signage legible, no unauthorised entry
monitoring.what_to_look_for: Barriers intact, signage legible, no unauthorised entry

hazards: Fall from height — worker on balcony during membrane application, particularly at edges

controls: Obtain and review SDS for membrane and primer before work starts; brief all workers on hazards, application method, and ventilation requirements.
Establish continuous mechanical ventilation across the slab during application and for 2 hours after; open all available windows and doors to occupied spaces below.
Apply membrane only in calm conditions — stop application if wind exceeds 15 km/h or if spray drift reaches occupied areas below.

Wear chemical-resistant gloves and eye protection; change gloves immediately if contact occurs.
Damp-wipe or cover wet membrane surfaces with non-slip matting to prevent slipping during cure; restrict worker movement to matting pathways only.
Install edge protection (aluminium angle or temporary mesh barrier) at all balcony edges and openings before membrane work starts; confirm no gaps or overlaps.
Rig full-body harness to certified anchor point before working within 2 m of any edge; do not remove harness until work in that zone is complete.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply screed until: Leo and Associates (engineer) has inspected and signed off membrane cure, bond strength, and test results per specification.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any worker shows signs of chemical exposure (nausea, dizziness, headache, eye irritation) — evacuate and seek medical advice immediately.
🛑 STOP WORK if: wind speed exceeds 15 km/h or spray reaches occupied areas; resume only when conditions improve.
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold tag is missing, expired, or handover certificate cannot be produced.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Brief workers on occupied building protocols; no application during peak hours 7–9 am, 5–6 pm.
Confirm EPA licence and waste disposal contractor details before delivery.
Record membrane lot number, application date, primer type, and cure completion in site diary.
Provide SDS and method statement to occupants 48 hours before work; post warning signs.
Arrange independent moisture and bond testing per engineer specification before hold point sign-off.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
ppe: P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) with organic vapour cartridge (type per SDS)
Full-body harness (certified, inspected, appropriate anchorage point)

monitoring.critical_control: SDS on site, PPE matched to chemical, ventilation confirmed
monitoring.frequency: start of each application shift and before each balcony zone entry
monitoring.evidence: Harness rigged to anchor point, cartridge installed, worker demonstrating fit and comfort of respirator

responsibility.SUP: Supervise membrane application, verify controls in place, sign off hold points and engineer inspection
responsibility.WKR: Apply membrane per SWMS, use PPE, report chemical exposure or hazards, comply with all controls

task_blocks_raw.scope: Apply screed to fall and finish. Retile balcony surfaces. Reinstate balustrades and edge trims to specification. Conduct final defect inspection before handover.
hazards: Fall from height — worker on balcony during screed placement, tiling or balustrade reinstallation, especially before balustrade completion
Struck by screed pump or tile saw — equipment malfunction, runaway hose or blade failure
Manual handling injury — lifting screed bags, tiles, balustrade panels or edge trims
Trip hazard from scaffold, wet screed, dropped tiles or temporary materials on balcony
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — worker on balcony during screed placement, tiling or balustrade reinstallation, especially before balustrade completion
controls: Verify scaffold handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder before any worker accesses balcony.
Confirm working at heights permit signed and current before starting screed, tiling or balustrade work.
Install perimeter edge protection (guardrail or certified fall arrest system) on all open edges before screed application.
Barricade wet screed and fresh tile surfaces with temporary fencing — keep exclusion zone 1m from wet edge.
Position screed pump on stable, level ground with pressure hose secured and checked for damage before each use.
Brief workers on wet slip hazard and trip risks from scaffold, hoses, dropped tiles and temporary materials at shift start.
Wear harness and lanyard attached to certified anchorage point when working within 2m of unprotected edge or incomplete balustrade.
Lift screed bags and tile boxes with mechanical aid where available — maximum 20kg manual load per worker.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply screed until: perimeter edge protection installed and inspected by supervisor.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not reinstate balustrade until: all screed and tile work complete and surfaces cured or set to specification.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: harness or lanyard detaches or damage visible during work at height.
🛑 STOP WORK if: screed pump hose ruptures, leaks pressurised product, or shows signs of failure.
🛑 STOP WORK if: balcony surface is saturated or slip risk is present and cannot be isolated.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain copy of scaffold erection permit and handover certificate — file on site before work starts.
Verify working at heights competency and white card current for all workers — names and expiry dates recorded.
Review SDS for screed membrane product — brief workers on handling, ventilation and skin contact controls.
Establish exclusion zone signage around wet screed and tiling work — inform building occupants of temporary access restrictions.
Conduct final defect inspection with supervisor — record on checklist: edge protection integrity, balustrade alignment, tile adhesion, trim finish, surface curing time.
ppe: Safety harness and certified lanyard (when working within 2m of unprotected edge)
Respirator or dust mask (P2 minimum when cutting dry tile or screed)

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: before each shift start and before each elevated task on balcony
monitoring.evidence: Scaffold tag visible, handover certificate on file, harness inspection log with date and worker initials

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Install screed, tiles and balustrades
responsibility.WKR: Perform Install screed, tiles and balustrades per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.task: Make good and reinstate occupied spaces
task_blocks_raw.scope: Remove protective coverings. Clean and reinstate common areas, access routes and courtyard. Remove temporary signage. Confirm occupant access fully restored and space safe for reoccupancy.
hazards: Occupant or worker struck by falling protective covering — inadequate removal or coverage collapse
Trip hazard from protective coverings, debris or temporary materials during reinstatement
Inadequate cleaning — dust, chemical residue or debris left on access routes or common areas hazards to occupants
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Occupant or worker struck by falling protective covering — inadequate removal or coverage collapse
controls: Remove protective coverings in sections — support each section before removing adjacent section to prevent collapse.
Lower each section of covering to ground using controlled descent — never drop or allow free fall.
Check coverings for tears, damage or contamination before removal — stop work if structural failure or hazmat suspected.
Sweep and vacuum all dust and debris from access routes and common areas before occupant return.
Wipe down hard surfaces in access routes with damp cloth to remove residual dust and chemical residue.
Remove all temporary signage, barricades and delineation markers from reinstated areas.
Brief occupants on any residual site activity or access restrictions before full handover.
Conduct final walk-through with site supervisor and occupant representative — confirm all hazards cleared and space safe for reoccupancy.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow occupant re-entry until: Site supervisor and occupant representative complete final walk-through and confirm all protective coverings removed, debris cleared, and hazards eliminated.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: protective covering shows signs of structural failure, tears, or collapse during removal.
🛑 STOP WORK if: chemical residue, visible contamination, or hazmat suspected on surfaces or coverings.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupants present in work area during removal of protective coverings or debris clearance.
admin: Obtain EPA licence confirmation before work starts — job involves removal of protective membranes in occupied building.
Confirm noise management plan in place and occupants notified of removal schedule.
Record final walk-through inspection and occupant sign-off on site diary.
Provide occupants with contact number for post-handover defect reporting.
ppe: Dust mask P2 — during sweeping and cleaning of residual dust

monitoring.frequency: before each rectification session
monitoring.evidence: Signed defect list, photographic record, specification document on site
monitoring.what_to_look_for: Signed defect list, photographic record, specification document on site

task_blocks_raw.scope: Dismantle and remove all scaffold from Kiora Lane and courtyard. Certification on removal. Leave site clear of all temporary structures.
hazards: Fall from height — worker falls during scaffold dismantling, particularly over Kiora Lane or courtyard
Scaffold collapse during dismantling — incomplete or incorrect removal sequence causes remaining structure instability
Struck by falling scaffold component — dropped tube, clamp, board or brace during removal
Pedestrian or vehicle struck on Kiora Lane — scaffold component falls or collapses onto traffic below
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — worker falls during scaffold dismantling, particularly over Kiora Lane or courtyard
controls: Obtain signed scaffold dismantling plan from licensed scaffolder before any removal starts.
Brief all workers on dismantling sequence and designated drop zones before work commences each day.
Barricade Kiora Lane below scaffold to exclude pedestrian and vehicle traffic during removal.
Remove scaffold components in reverse erection sequence — top to bottom, working from one end.
Secure each removed component immediately to prevent rolling or shifting on platform.
Tag removed scaffold as 'unsafe for reuse' if bent, cracked or deformed.
Lower all components to ground using rope and pulley — do not drop or throw.
Verify all fixings and connections are released before moving or removing any component.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start dismantling until: licensed scaffolder has reviewed site conditions and signed dismantling plan
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove final components until: licensed scaffolder has inspected remaining structure for stability and signed removal certificate
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any component falls or is dropped onto Kiora Lane or occupied areas below
🛑 STOP WORK if: remaining scaffold shows visible movement, sag, twist or cracking during removal
🛑 STOP WORK if: barricade or exclusion zone is breached by pedestrian or vehicle traffic
admin: Obtain and verify signed scaffold dismantling plan from licensed scaffolder before work start.
Verify all workers hold current White Card and Scaffolding Licence appropriate to scaffold class and height.
Verify all workers hold current Working at Heights competency (RIIOHS204E or equivalent).
Brief site occupants on dismantling schedule, noise, and exclusion zones 24 hours before work.
Record daily dismantling progress, any structural concerns, and licensed scaffolder inspections in site diary.
Obtain and file final removal certificate from licensed scaffolder confirming all scaffold removed and site clear.
ppe: Wear full-body harness with inertia reel lanyard secured to fixed anchor point — test anchor before use.
Wear steel-capped boots with ankle support.

monitoring.critical_control: Licensed scaffolder verifies dismantling sequence and remaining structure stability daily.
monitoring.frequency: Before each day's removal work and before final sign-off
monitoring.evidence: Signed dismantling plan, daily inspection notes, final removal certificate filed

responsibility.SUP: Verify scaffold or EWP certification, supervise erection, sign off load checks
responsibility.WKR: Follow erection plan, wear harness at height, report defects

task_blocks_raw.scope: Remove site office, welfare facilities and all plant. Dispose of waste. Final site inspection and sign-off. Restore Kiora Lane and courtyard to pre-works condition.
hazards: Manual handling injury — removing site office, welfare facility components, plant or waste materials
Vehicle struck or struck by vehicle — plant movement in confined Kiora Lane or courtyard during removal
Trip hazard from temporary structures, plant or waste during demobilisation
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Manual handling injury — removing site office, welfare facility components, plant or waste materials
controls: Plan removal sequence with Site Supervisor before starting — identify heavy items, access routes, and staging areas in Kiora Lane and courtyard
Barricade Kiora Lane and courtyard to exclude vehicles and occupants during plant movement and waste removal
Brief all workers on manual handling before removing site office or welfare components — use team lift for items over 20 kg
Use mechanical handling (forklift, telehandler or crane) for items over 50 kg — do not hand-carry large panels, furniture or equipment
Load waste into skip bin or licensed waste truck — confirm waste type matches EPA disposal requirements before removal from site
Clear temporary structures, cables, hoses and debris from all walking areas before final inspection — remove trip hazards
Conduct final walkover of Kiora Lane and courtyard with Site Supervisor and building occupant representative — photograph pre-works condition baseline for comparison
Restore Kiora Lane and courtyard surfaces to pre-works condition — repair damage, remove temporary markings, clean dust and debris
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove site office or welfare facility until: Site Supervisor confirms all hazardous materials (asbestos, lead, chemicals) have been identified and removed by licensed contractor if applicable

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not sign off final inspection until: building occupant representative and Site Supervisor confirm Kiora Lane and courtyard match pre-works condition, and all plant, waste and temporary structures are removed

Record final site inspection photographs and sign-off sheet — Site Supervisor and building occupant representative signatures required
Verify all plant, temporary structures and waste removed from Kiora Lane and courtyard before site vacation
Confirm all utilities (power, water, temporary services) isolated and disabled — record on site handover form
